$comment: The badge kit of one repository (FS04-031, WEB-084; ops decision D115, slices P13b and P16a): what a repository's administrator pastes into a README, and the addresses of the repository's project cards. Two implementations compose it from the same three inputs, the dashboard's api in C# and the website's registry page in JavaScript, and each is held to this file member for member and character for character, so a snippet copied from the dashboard and one copied from the repository's public page are the same text.

`input` is the repository's GitHub node id, the origin the edge answers on and the public site's origin. `kit` is the answer. `endpoint`, `markdown` and `html` are the shields.io endpoint (`/badge/{nodeId}.json`) and its two snippets. `page` is the registry page every snippet links to. `flat` and `card` are the repository's own badges (openapi/edge-public.v1.yaml `getRepositoryBadge`): the flat badge, and the 420×88 card in a light and a dark version, whose HTML is one `<picture>` that shows the dark version under `prefers-color-scheme: dark`; Markdown cannot switch, so the card's Markdown shows the light one. `projectCard` (1200×630) and `socialPreview` (1280×640, for GitHub's repository social preview) are the project cards (`getRepositoryCard`).
Every snippet names the canonical hosts verbatim (CERT-027). A snippet changes here first, and then in both implementations in the same release.
